transcript.text: Hi Test: Honest junior, this is Donna, an AI assistant calling for Alex at Acme (demo). This call is recorded. I saw your work on a Redis-backed rate limiter library. Got a few minutes for a quick screen for the Founding Engineer role?
Great, thanks. Your rate limiter claims 50k requests per second. How did you measure that, and what broke first?
I built a smaller version of a Redis rate limiter for a side project, a sliding window with a sorted set, but I never measured anything close to 50k requests per second.
Got it, thanks for being straight about that. What did you actually measure, even roughly, and what was the first thing that gave out when you pushed it?
Honestly I only tested it with a few hundred requests a second from a local script, so I can't tell you where it would break first.
Thanks, that's useful to know. Next question: on the payments team, what went wrong with idempotency keys, and how did you find out?
I haven't worked on a payments team; I've only read the payments code in an open source project, where the idempotency key was stored with the response so a retry returned the same result.
Thanks for clarifying that. Last question: if you joined tomorrow, what would you want to own in your first two weeks?
In my first two weeks I'd pair with someone on the API, fix a couple of small bugs, and learn how deploys and monitoring work before owning anything bigger.
Thanks, Test: Honest junior. I'll pass my notes to Alex, and you'll get a calendar invite if they'd like to meet.
Thanks again for your time, and good luck. Goodbye.

elevenLabsAnalysis.transcript_summary: The AI agent conducted a screening call for a Founding Engineer role. The agent inquired about the user's Redis-backed rate limiter performance, to which the user clarified they only tested it locally at a lower scale and couldn't identify a breaking point. The user also clarified they hadn't worked on a payments team regarding idempotency keys but had read relevant open-source code. For their first two weeks, the user expressed interest in pairing on the API, fixing small bugs, and learning about deploys and monitoring. The agent concluded by stating notes would be passed on for potential next steps.
